newsitem.title: CHINA: Thai death toll in China air crash rises.
newsitem.headline: Thai death toll in China air crash rises.

text.p: The number of Thais killed when a China Southern Airlines Boeing 737-300 crashed while trying to land during a thunderstorm in the southern city of Shenzhen has risen to 21, airline officials said on Saturday.
Officials orginally indicated 16 Thai tourists died in Thursday's crash, but the official said the number had been raised to 21. He did not give any details.
He declined to say how many foreigners were among the 35 people killed when China Southern flight CZ3456 slammed into the tarmac of Shenzhen's storm-swept airport.
The Thai nationals were among a group of 25 tourists on board the aircraft, which broke into three pieces and burst into flames on impact.
Thirty-five people are known to have survived the accident, while another four were still unaccounted for on Saturday.

The airline official, reached by telephone in Shenzhen, just over the border from Hong Kong, declined to give the identities of the Thais who died. The Thai embassy in Beijing could not be reached for comment.
One aviation official has said the aircraft crashed after trying twice to land during a storm that lashed southern China on Thursday.
A Hong Kong man who survived told reporters from his hospital bed that the Boeing's pilot had ordered passengers to sit near the centre of the aircraft shortly before it crashed.
Two of those killed in the accident, China's first big aviation disaster in nearly three years, were members of the aircraft's crew and included the co-pilot, officials have said.
But there were diverging reports of exactly how many people were on board the aircraft and the extent of the injuries to those that survived.

Some officials said the three-year-old Boeing 737-300 was carrying 65 passengers and nine crew from the southwestern city of Chongqing, but the official Xinhua news agency said there were only eight crew.
Officials have said nine of the injured were in critical condition, while Xinhua put the number of critically injured at three. It said 10 people escaped injury.
One Hong Kong resident and two Taiwanese were among the injured, one of whom was in critical condition, officials said.
Rescue workers have found its "black box" flight recorder, and both the plane's maker Boeing and the Civil Aviation Administration of China have sent teams to probe the disaster.

Before the crash Chinese aviation officials had been celebrating almost three years without a serious air accident, a record credited to improved precautions taken after a Russian-made Tupolev-154 exploded after takeoff in 1994, killing 160 people.
